children.translated_text: First chapter.

children.text: śṛṅgārī girijānane sakaruṇo ratyāṃ pravīraḥ smare
children.translated_text: Amorous (<s>śṛṅgārin</s>) toward the face of <s>Girijā</s> (Pārvatī), compassionate in love, heroic (<s>pravīra</s>) in passion (<s>Smara</s>),

children.text: bībhatso'sthibhir utphaṇī ca bhaya-kṛn mūrtyādbhutas tuṅgayā
children.translated_text: odious (<s>bībhatsa</s>) with bones, with raised hood and terror-inspiring, wondrous (<s>adbhuta</s>) in his towering form,

children.text: raudro dakṣa-vimardane ca hasakṛn nagnaḥ praśāntaś cirād
children.translated_text: furious (<s>raudra</s>) in the destruction of <s>Dakṣa</s>, laughing while naked, and serene (<s>praśānta</s>) for ages —

children.text: itthaṃ sarva-rasāśrayaḥ paśupatir bhūyāt satāṃ bhūtaye
children.translated_text: thus, may <s>Paśupati</s> (Śiva), the abode of all <s>rasas</s>, be for the welfare of the virtuous.
With well-formed composition of verbs and nouns, well-joined <s>sandhis</s>,
endowed with the quality of fine speech and ornamentation, juicy and of excellent meter —
even of those foremost poets who have reached heaven,
their body made of poetry remains unbroken here [on earth].

children.text: kāvye śubhe'pi racite khalu no khalebhyaḥ
children.translated_text: Even when a fine poem is composed, no merit comes from the wicked;
even though [this is so] now,

children.text: kṛpāṃ tathāpi sujanārtham idaṃ yataḥ kiṃ
children.translated_text: yet, out of compassion, this is [composed] for the sake of the virtuous — for why
should one abandon clothing for fear of lice?
Those whose minds are not pierced by the arrow-like sidelong glances of joyful women,
who have ferried across others sinking in the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>,
who have contained the boundless play of <s>Sarasvatī</s> (eloquence) in just two or three words —

children.text: teṣām apy upari sphuranti matayaḥ kasyāpi puṇyātmanaḥ
children.translated_text: even above them shine the thoughts of some blessed soul.
The doctrine of <s>rasa</s> has been mostly expounded
by <s>Bharata</s> and others with respect to drama (<s>nāṭya</s>);
to the best of my understanding, this same [doctrine]
is here set forth with respect to poetry (<s>kāvya</s>).
Like a night without the moon,
like a woman without her lover,
like <s>Lakṣmī</s> without generosity —
speech does not shine when devoid of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text: satyaṃ santi gṛhe gṛhe sukavayo yeṣāṃ vacaś cāturī
children.translated_text: Truly, in every household there are good poets whose verbal skill

children.text: sve harmye kula-kanyakeva labhate jātair guṇair gauravam
children.translated_text: gains esteem through innate qualities, like a well-born maiden in her own mansion;

children.text: duṣprāpaḥ sa tu ko'pi kovida-patir yad vāg-rasa-grāhiṇāṃ
children.translated_text: but rare is that master among the learned whose speech, skilled in the arts and their varieties,
like a virtuous woman, is capable of captivating the hearts of those who appreciate the <s>rasas</s> of speech.
Therefore, one should compose poetry
with diligent effort, permeated with <s>rasa</s>;
otherwise, even a learned man's [composition], in an assembly,
would cause discomfort.
<s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic), <s>hāsya</s> (comic), <s>karuṇā</s> (pathetic),
<s>raudra</s> (furious), <s>vīra</s> (heroic), <s>bhayānaka</s> (terrible),
<s>bībhatsa</s> (odious), <s>adbhuta</s> (wondrous), and <s>śānta</s> (quiescent) —
these nine are recognized as the <s>rasas</s> in poetry.
<s>Rati</s> (love), <s>hāsa</s> (mirth), <s>śoka</s> (sorrow),
<s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>utsāha</s> (enthusiasm), <s>bhaya</s> (fear),
<s>jugupsā</s> (disgust), <s>vismaya</s> (wonder), and <s>śama</s> (tranquility) —
these are proclaimed as the <s>sthāyibhāvas</s> (permanent emotions).
<s>Nirveda</s> (despondency), <s>glāni</s> (languor),
<s>śaṅkā</s> (apprehension), <s>asūyā</s> (envy), <s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>śrama</s> (fatigue),
<s>ālasya</s> (laziness), <s>dainya</s> (wretchedness),
<s>cintā</s> (anxiety), <s>moha</s> (delusion), <s>dhṛti</s> (fortitude), <s>smṛti</s> (recollection),
<s>vrīḍā</s> (bashfulness), <s>capalatā</s> (fickleness), <s>harṣa</s> (joy),
<s>āvega</s> (agitation), <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor),
<s>garva</s> (pride), <s>viṣāda</s> (despondency), <s>autsukyā</s> (eagerness),
<s>nidrā</s> (sleep), and <s>apasmāra</s> (epileptic fit),
<s>supta</s> (dreaming), <s>prabodha</s> (awakening), <s>amarṣa</s> (indignation),
<s>avahitthā</s> (dissimulation), and <s>ugratā</s> (ferocity),
<s>mati</s> (resolve), <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), <s>unmāda</s> (madness),
and <s>maraṇa</s> (death),
<s>trāsa</s> (fright) and <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) —
these should be known as the <s>vyabhicāribhāvas</s> (transitory emotions).
These thirty-three <s>bhāvas</s>
enter into the condition of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Stambha</s> (stupefaction), <s>sveda</s> (perspiration), <s>romāñca</s> (horripilation),
<s>svarabhāṅga</s> (voice-breaking), <s>vepathu</s> (trembling),
<s>vaivarṇya</s> (discoloration), <s>aśru</s> (tears), and <s>pralaya</s> (fainting) —
these eight are recognized as the <s>sāttvikabhāvas</s> (involuntary reactions).
These very <s>bhāvas</s>, when fully developed,
attain the state of <s>rasa</s> —
just as different substances
partake of the nature of sweet and other flavors.
Just as on a tree
flowers, leaves, fruits, and so forth arise,
so too in <s>rasa</s>, the beautiful
distinctions take the form of <s>bhāvas</s>.
For the most part, no poem is found
that consists of a single <s>rasa</s>;
whichever [<s>rasa</s>] predominates,
that is designated according to its <s>vṛtti</s> (style).
<s>Kaiśikī</s>, <s>ārabhaṭī</s>,
<s>sātvatī</s>, and <s>bhāratī</s> —
these four <s>vṛttis</s> (styles) should be known
as indicators of the predominance of [particular] <s>rasas</s>.
From <s>dharma</s> comes <s>artha</s>, from <s>artha</s> comes <s>kāma</s>,
from <s>kāma</s> arises the fruit of happiness;
most excellent for the attainment of these is
<s>śṛṅgāra</s>, the chief <s>rasa</s>.
The behavior that arises between man and woman
when <s>rati</s> (love) is aroused to excess —
<s>saṃyoga</s> (union) and <s>vipralambha</s> (separation) —
<s>śṛṅgāra</s> is regarded as twofold.
<s>Saṃyoga</s> is [the state] of those who are united,
<s>vipralambha</s> of those who are separated;
and this again is twofold —
concealed (<s>pracchanna</s>) and manifest (<s>prakāśa</s>).
On the pair of breasts resembling the temples of the elephant of <s>Madana</s> (Kāma),
with fingers spread all around,
though her beloved's hand was scratched with nail-marks on the left,
the beloved considered it auspicious [lit. right-handed/dakṣiṇa].
Tormented by involuntary sighs arising from love's assemblage, the fifth

children.text: dgārāvartibhir āpatadbhir abhitaḥ siktaś ca netrāmbubhiḥ
children.translated_text: [breath] whirling out in spirals, sprinkled on all sides with tears from the eyes —
distressed by separation from the beloved, her lower lip having lost its color,
I think she now observes the difficult vow of fire, water, and [their] opposition.
Though the beloved, with her fawn-like eyes, was absorbed in the varied sequence of lovemaking,
at the trysting place as well,
her certain cooing [was so sweet] that her couch
was surrounded by no small number of answering quails.
With her neck slightly bent, her full breasts bursting through
the tightly drawn bodice — that gaze of the doe-eyed one,

children.text: vācas tāś ca vidagdha-bhāva-caturāḥ sphārībhavan manmathā
children.translated_text: and those words, clever with the ways of sophistication, expanding the passion of love —

children.text: haṃho mānasa kiṃ smarasy abhimatāḥ siddhyanti puṇyaiḥ kriyāḥ
children.translated_text: Alas, O mind, why do you remember? Desired deeds are accomplished through merit.
Generous, well-born, skilled in love,
capable, versed in arts, young, wealthy,
handsome, patient, fortunate, and proud —

children.text: strīṇām abhīṣṭas tv iha nāyakaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: such should be the hero (<s>nāyaka</s>) desired by women.
His [types are] the <s>anukūla</s> (faithful), <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (courteous), <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful), and <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold) — thus four
types are described through their actions, with charming illustrations.
Due to extreme attachment to one woman, always forsaking other women,

children.text: sītāyāṃ rāmavat so'yam anukūlaḥ smṛto yathā //
children.translated_text: like <s>Rāma</s> toward <s>Sītā</s> — this one is known as the <s>anukūla</s> (faithful), as follows:

children.text: asmākaṃ sakhi vāsasī na rucire graiveyakaṃ nojjvalaṃ
children.translated_text: O friend, our garments are not lovely, the necklace does not sparkle,

children.text: no vaktrā gatir uddhataṃ na hasitaṃ naivāsti kaścin madaḥ
children.translated_text: neither is the gait of the face haughty, nor the laughter — there is no intoxication at all;

children.text: kiṃ tv anye'pi janā vadanti subhago'py asyāḥ priyo nānyato
children.translated_text: yet other people say: 'Even though her beloved is handsome, she does not',

children.text: dṛṣṭiṃ niḥkṣipatīti viśvam iyatā manyāmahe duḥkhitam
children.translated_text: 'cast her glance elsewhere' — by this much alone we consider the whole world to be suffering.
He who does not abandon respect, fear, love,
and genuine affection toward his former wife,
even though his mind is [attracted] elsewhere —
he is to be known as the <s>dakṣiṇa</s> (courteous), as follows:

children.text: saivāsya praṇatis tad eva vacanaṃ tā eva keli-kriyā
children.translated_text: The same obeisance, the same words, the same amorous play,

children.text: bhītiḥ saiva tad eva narma-madhuraṃ pūrvānurāgocitam
children.translated_text: the same timidity, the same sweet jesting befitting the former love —
'You say the beloved does her wrong' — [yet] you call him full of faults;

children.text: kiṃ syād ittham aharniśaṃ sakhi mano dolāyate cintayā
children.translated_text: what could this be? Day and night, O friend, the mind swings on the pendulum of thought.
He who speaks sweetly in one's presence
but acts disagreeably elsewhere,
whose behavior shows known offenses —
that crooked one is the <s>śaṭha</s> (deceitful), as follows:
O naturally fickle one, we both are indeed rich in much learning;

children.text: punar iha yuvāṃ satyaṃ śiṣṭaṃ tad atra kṛtāgasi
children.translated_text: then again, you two — truly, 'that is proper'; in this, you are the offender;

children.text: praṇayini punar yuktaṃ rantuṃ na veti batāvayo
children.translated_text: yet with the beloved, whether it is right to sport or not — alas,

children.text: rdhruvam upagate karṇau praṣṭuṃ kuraṅga-dṛśau dṛśau
children.translated_text: when [the matter] has surely reached the ears, the fawn-eyed ones have [only] the eyes to ask.
Moreover —

children.text: kopāt kiñcid upānato'pi rabhasād ākṛṣya keśeṣv alaṃ
children.translated_text: Though slightly bent forward in anger, seized forcibly by the hair,

children.text: nītvā mohana-mandiraṃ dayitayā hāreṇa bahvā dṛḍham
children.translated_text: firmly led to the chamber of love by the beloved with a garland,

children.text: bhūyo yāsyasi tad-gṛhān iti muhuḥ kaṇṭhāruddhākṣaraṃ
children.translated_text: while she utters with choked words at the throat 'You will go to her house again!' —

children.text: jalpantyā śravaṇotpalena sukṛtī kaścid rahas tāḍyate
children.translated_text: some fortunate man is struck in secret with a lotus from behind her ear.
Shameless even when at fault,
unabashed even when rebuked,
a liar even when his fault is seen —
such a one is called the <s>dhṛṣṭa</s> (bold), as follows:

children.text: jalpantyāḥ paruṣaṃ ruṣā mama balāc cumbaty asāv ānanaṃ
children.translated_text: While she speaks harshly in anger, he forcibly kisses her face;

children.text: mṛd-gātyāśu karaṃ kareṇa bahuśaḥ santāḍyamāno'pi san
children.translated_text: though repeatedly struck on the hand with her own hand, he still rubs her gently;

children.text: ālīnāṃ purato dadhāti śirasā pāda-prahārāṃs tato
children.translated_text: he bears blows of her foot upon his head before her friends —

children.text: no jāne sakhi sāmprataṃ praṇayien kupyāmi tasmai katham
children.translated_text: I know not, O friend, whether I should now be affectionate or angry with him.
Moreover —

children.text: dhik tvām dhūrta gata-trapa praṇayinī saiva tvayārādhyatā
children.translated_text: 'Shame on you, rogue, shameless one! Go worship that same beloved

children.text: yasyāḥ pāda-talāhatiṃ tava hṛdi vyākhyāty asau yāvakaḥ
children.translated_text: whose foot-sole's imprint on your chest this lac-dye proclaims!'

children.text: ity ukto'pi na nāma muñcati yadā pādāv ayaṃ durjano
children.translated_text: Though told thus, when this wicked man does not release her feet,

children.text: mithyāvāda-vicakṣaṇaḥ kim aparaṃ kuryāṃ vayasye tadā
children.translated_text: O friend, what more can I do, [being] expert in false words?
One who keeps secrets, is pure, eloquent,
devoted, and skilled in jesting —
such should be his confidant (<s>narmasaciva</s>),
one who pacifies the angered women.
<s>Pīṭhamarda</s>, <s>viṭa</s>, and
<s>vidūṣaka</s> — these are the three [types];
of these, the first
follows both the heroine and the hero.
The <s>viṭa</s> is said to be skilled in one art;
the <s>vidūṣaka</s> is mainly for sport,
creating laughter through his own appearance, dress, and speech,
and is a jester.

children.text: eṣāṃ prabandha-viṣayo vyavahāraḥ prāyaśo bhavet pracuraḥ &
children.translated_text: Their involvement in the plot is generally extensive;
though [examples have been] individually cited, some are [now] stated.

children.text: vimuñcāmuṃ mānaṃ saphalaya vacaḥ sādhu suhṛdāṃ
children.translated_text: Abandon this pique, fulfill the good words of friends;

children.text: mudhā santāpena glapayasi kim aṅgaṃ smara-bhuvā
children.translated_text: why do you pointlessly waste your body with sorrow born of love?
Honor now the beloved who bows at your feet;

children.text: na mugdhe pretyetuṃ prabhavati gataḥ kāla-hariṇaḥ
children.translated_text: O innocent one, the deer-like time that has gone cannot return.

children.text: praṇayini bhṛśaṃ tasmin mānaṃ manasvini mā kṛthāḥ
children.translated_text: O proud one, do not maintain this pique toward that loving man;

children.text: kim aparam ito yuktāyuktair vinā hy amunā tava
children.translated_text: what more [can be said] — without him, with or without propriety, for you

children.text: ayam api bhavet sampraty api kṣayānala-saṃnibhaḥ
children.translated_text: even this [moon] now resembles the fire of dissolution,
though it has the hue of a fresh lotus-stalk cut, and bears the mark of a deer [i.e., the moon].

children.text: dūrāt kandalitair hṛdi pravitataiḥ kaṇṭhe luṭhadbhir haṭhā
children.translated_text: With sighs that kindle from afar within the heart, roll forcibly along the throat,
and emerge from the constrained, trembling nostrils of the face,
the fever of intense passion has clearly been announced —

children.text: mthyālambita-sauṣṭhavena kim ataḥ kopena kāntaṃ prati
children.translated_text: then what use is this falsely assumed composure, this anger toward the beloved?
One's own (<s>svakīyā</s>), another's (<s>parakīyā</s>),
and the common woman (<s>sāmānyā</s>) —
skilled in the arts and their varieties,
these are his three heroines (<s>nāyikās</s>).
Devoted to proper civic conduct, virtuous,
adorned with patience and uprightness —
<s>mugdhā</s> (naive), <s>madhyā</s> (moderate), and <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold) —
the <s>svakīyā</s> (one's own wife) is regarded as threefold.
The <s>mugdhā</s> is there the newly married bride,
adorned with fresh youth,
new to the secrets of love —
her delight is mostly bashfulness, as follows:
[Youth] has reached near her ears, yet the pair of eyes still spreads [wide in innocence];
her breasts are beginning to swell like water-pots, yet she still delights in tilting her chin up;
her heavy hips have already gained weight, yet seek [still more] heaviness —

children.text: kathaṃcin no tṛptis taruṇimani manye mṛga-dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: somehow there is no satisfaction in the youth of the doe-eyed one, I think.
As this horripilation on the region of the breasts, with glistening drops of perspiration,

children.text: yathā dṛṣṭis tiryak patati sahasā saṅkucati ca
children.translated_text: as the glance falls sideways suddenly and contracts —
so I suspect that her heart, having slightly tasted the flavor of love,

children.text: na madhyasthaṃ cetaḥ praguṇa-ramaṇīyaṃ na ca dṛḍham
children.translated_text: is neither indifferent nor yet fully developed and firm.
'Desist, my lord, release my garment-edge,
extinguish the lamp — here comes my friend' —
by such words of the newly-wed bride, the young man
attained a joy greater even than lovemaking.
Trembling, she turns away her face when kissed;
when embraced, she withdraws;
turning away for a long time on the bed,
yet she desires to make love.
When she turns away her face at a kiss while being embraced,

children.text: valati ca śayanīye kampate ca prakāmam
children.translated_text: and turns on the bed and trembles greatly,

children.text: vadati ca yad alakṣyaṃ kiñcid uktāpi bhūyo
children.translated_text: and says something inaudible even when spoken to again —
the newly-wed bride delights the mind all the more within.
He wins over the <s>mugdhā</s>
with gentle means, soothing her,
with sentiments not overly frightening,
with [binding] techniques that are childishly alarming.
'This swarm of buzzing bees is moving away from the lake-shore;
O fair-faced one, I think the bee, being hostile to the lotus, [comes] thirsting for your face' —
when this was said, with her neck slightly turned out of fear,
the young bride was long kissed on her lotus-face by her husband.
Even when the beloved attends to another woman,
if she [the naive one] is angry,
she weeps briefly in his presence,
and when consoled, is satisfied.

children.text: manyau kṛte prathamam eva vikāram anyaṃ
children.translated_text: When the pique is first aroused, the newly-wed bride

children.text: no jānatī nava-vadhū rudatī paraṃ sā
children.translated_text: knows no other emotion — she only weeps;
by the rogue, her tears are wiped away, she is firmly
kissed on the lower lip, and brought to satisfaction.
The <s>madhyā</s> (moderate) is one whose youth is fully arrived,
in whom love has manifested,
somewhat bold in speech,
with varied lovemaking — as follows:

children.text: tarat-tāraṃ cakṣuḥ kṣapayati munīnām api dṛśaḥ
children.translated_text: With sparkling wide eyes, she destroys even the gaze of sages;
the pair of breasts having seized the heart — who of heartless men would not be moved?
Her gait, having become slow, captivates the movement of those possessed by love;

children.text: maho tanvyās tulyaṃ taruṇimani sarvaṃ vijayate
children.translated_text: O how equally in youth everything triumphs over this slender one!

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ snihyati nirbharaṃ priyatame vaidagdhya-bhājo giraḥ
children.translated_text: The gaze melts with deep affection for her beloved; her words are marked by cleverness;
her hand, abandoning all other tasks, is engaged in arranging locks and garlands;

children.text: vakṣaḥ saṃvriyate punaḥ punar idaṃ bhārālasaṃ gamyate
children.translated_text: her bosom is covered again and again; she walks with heaviness and languor —

children.text: jātā subhru manoramā tava daśā kasmād akasmād iyam
children.translated_text: O fair-browed one, this charming state of yours has arisen — from what, and so suddenly?

children.text: subhaga kuravakas tvaṃ no kim āliṅganoktiḥ
children.translated_text: 'You are a handsome <s>kuravaka</s> tree — what is this talk of embracing?

children.text: kim u mukhamadirecchuḥ kesaro no hṛdisthaḥ
children.translated_text: Are you a <s>kesara</s> flower, thirsting for the wine of [my] lips? No, you dwell in [my] heart!
Surely with you, O <s>aśoka</s> tree, a kick of the foot is appropriate!'

children.text: priyam iti parihāsāt peśalaṃ kācid ūce
children.translated_text: Thus a certain woman spoke playfully to her beloved, in jest.

children.text: kānte tathā katham api prathitaṃ mṛgākṣyā
children.translated_text: In such a manner, the doe-eyed one somehow manifested to her beloved
her skill in lovemaking, aroused by passion —
as though hundreds of household pigeons, imitating her cooing
again and again, had become her pupils.
She engages her beloved tightly
in lovemaking, like one possessed by an elephant,
as if entering into his limbs,
as if swooning in pleasure.

children.text: kṛtvāneka-vidhāṃ rasena surate keliṃ kathañcic cirā
children.translated_text: Having performed manifold amorous play with <s>rasa</s> (passion) in lovemaking, somehow at last
arriving at the conclusion, with both eyes half-closed in pleasure, her temple-region perspiring —

children.text: supteyaṃ kila sundarīti subhagaḥ svairaṃ tathaivāsvaja
children.translated_text: 'This beautiful woman is indeed asleep!' — thinking thus, the fortunate one freely embraced her just so,
and his body unable to endure the intense friction of passion, he arrived at sleep together [with her].
The steadfast one (<s>dhīrā</s>) addresses her beloved, who has committed an offense, with indirect speech born of anger;
the moderate one (<s>madhyā</s>) weeps with reproaches;
the impetuous one (<s>adhīrā</s>) [speaks] harshly —
as follows:
Having approached her, long eager for a tight embrace,
with lovely sandal-paste wiped away [by her struggle],
bearing collyrium [now smeared] from kissing her eyes —
'Here and now, O beloved, your fulfillment is made known [to me]!'
'Where the moon has been made a sun by [your] lotuses, where [your eyes have become] heaps of embers,

children.text: kruddhāyāṃ mayi nātha te kadalikākāṇḍair alātāyitam
children.translated_text: when you are angry with me, O lord, where the plantain-stalks have become firebrands —

children.text: kālo'nyaḥ khalu ko'pi so'mṛtamayo jāto viṣātmādhunā
children.translated_text: surely that was some other time, now become nectar-filled, [which] has now become poison —

children.text: dhik tvāṃ dhūrta viniryad-aśrur abalā mohaṃ rudantī gatā
children.translated_text: Shame on you, rogue!' — with tears flowing forth, the helpless woman, weeping, fell into a swoon.
'Together with a hundred desires, O rogue, that very beloved
of yours remains in your mind, charming with artificial sentiments!

children.text: asmākam asti na hi kaścid ihāvakāśas
children.translated_text: For us there is no place here at all —
therefore, enough of these mockeries of falling at my feet!'
The <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold woman) is one who has attained maturity,
skilled in all forms of lovemaking,
a dominant heroine (<s>ākrāntanāyikā</s>) indeed,
shining with resplendent coquetry — as follows:

children.text: seyaṃ paraṅginī mṛṇāla-latikām ādāya yasyāḥ priyo
children.translated_text: 'This is she, O friend, that other woman, taking a lotus-fiber tendril, whose beloved
makes a necklace on the slope of my breasts with the freshness of new stars!

children.text: bandhūkaṃ ca tad etad āli vidalad yat tena sīmantitaṃ
children.translated_text: And this <s>bandhūka</s> flower — see how it blooms — which he has placed as a parting-ornament!
It will bear the beauty of the arrows of the flower-bowed [<s>Kāma</s>], who conquers all desires!'

children.text: yatra sveda-lavair alaṃ vlulitair vyālupyate candanaṃ
children.translated_text: Where the sandal-paste is smeared away by scattered drops of sweat,

children.text: svacchandair maṇitaiś ca yatra raṇitaṃ nihnūyate nūpuram
children.translated_text: where the anklets are drowned out by unchecked moans,
where all the senses quickly reach single-pointed absorption in that [pleasure] —

children.text: sakhyas tat-surataṃ bhaṇāmi rataye śeṣā tu loka-sthitiḥ
children.translated_text: O friends, I declare that lovemaking [to be supreme]; the rest is mere worldly existence!

children.text: svāmin bhaṅgurayālakaṃ sa-tilakaṃ bhālaṃ vilāsin kuru
children.translated_text: 'O lord, make my forehead beautiful with a <s>tilaka</s> (ornamental mark) and curling locks!

children.text: prāṇeśa truṭitaṃ payodhara-taṭe hāraṃ punar yojaya
children.translated_text: O master of my life, re-fasten the broken necklace on the slope of my breasts!'
Having thus spoken, delighted at the conclusion of lovemaking, with a face full like the moon,

children.text: spṛṣṭā tena tatheti jāta-pulakā prāptā punar mohanam
children.translated_text: touched by him [saying] 'So be it!' — she, with horripilation arising, attained the swoon [of passion] again.
With sweet words, with brow-movements, with playful finger-wagging,
with languid turnings of limbs that are companions to great festivity,
with broadly expansive sidelong glances again and again —
she renders assistance to the five-arrowed [<s>Kāma</s>] in conquering the three worlds.
This one, unperturbed in lovemaking,
melts as it were into the beloved's body —
'Who is he? Who am I? What is lovemaking?'
She knows not, from [excess of] passion — as follows:

children.text: dhanyās tāḥ sakhi yoṣitaḥ priyatame sarvāṅga-lagne'pi yāḥ
children.translated_text: 'Blessed are those women, O friend, who even when the beloved clings to every limb,

children.text: prāgalbhyaṃ prathayanti mohana-vidhāv ālambya dhairyaṃ mahat
children.translated_text: display boldness in the art of enchantment, maintaining great composure!
But for us, when his lotus-hand merely loosens our garment,

children.text: ko'yaṃ kā vayam atra kiṃ nu surataṃ naiva smṛtir jāyate
children.translated_text: "Who is he? Who am I? What is lovemaking here?" — not even memory arises!'
Even when he has committed an offense, the steadfast one (<s>dhīrā</s>)
does not heed him in anger;
she conceals her feelings
and remains composed in lovemaking — as follows:

children.text: yad vācaḥ pracuropacāra-caturā yat sādaraṃ dūrataḥ
children.translated_text: 'That your words are excessively skillful in courtesies; that there is this rising from afar with respect;

children.text: pratyutthānam idaṃ svahasta-nihitaṃ yad-bhinnam apy āsanam
children.translated_text: that a separate seat is placed by your own hand;

children.text: utpaśyāmi yad evam eva ca muhur dṛṣṭiṃ sakhī-saṃmukhīṃ
children.translated_text: that I observe your gaze thus repeatedly directed toward [my] friend —

children.text: tac chaṅke tava paṅkajākṣi balavān ko'py aprasādo mayi
children.translated_text: from all this I suspect, O lotus-eyed one, some powerful displeasure toward me on your part.'

children.text: yat pāṇir na nivārito nivasana-granthiṃ saumudgranthaya
children.translated_text: 'That the hand was not restrained while eagerly untying the knot of the garment;

children.text: nbhrū-bhedo na kṛto manāg api muhur yat-khaṇḍyamāne'dhare
children.translated_text: that the brow was not furrowed even slightly while the lip was being repeatedly bitten;

children.text: yan niḥśaṅkam ivārpitaṃ vapur aho patyuḥ samāliṅgane
children.translated_text: that the body was yielded as if without suspicion to the husband's embrace —
by the proud woman's own accommodating behavior, that very great anger was declared!'
The moderate one (<s>madhyā</s>) reproaches him
with well-spoken words mixed with mockery;
the impetuous one (<s>adhīrā</s>) strikes the beloved
with threats delivered through men — as follows:

children.text: kṛtaṃ mithyā-jalpair virama viditaṃ kāmuka cirāt
children.translated_text: 'Enough of false prattling! Desist! It has long been known, O lover!

children.text: priyāṃ tām evoccair abhisara yadīyair nakha-padaiḥ
children.translated_text: Go loudly and visit that very beloved of yours, by whose nail-marks

children.text: vilāsaiś ca prāptaṃ tava hṛdi padaṃ raga-bahulair
children.translated_text: and coquetries a place has been won in your heart, [a heart] abundant with passion!

children.text: mayā kiṃ te kṛtyaṃ dhruvam akuṭilācāra-parayā
children.translated_text: What is your business with me, who am ever devoted to straight conduct?'

children.text: sā bāḍhaṃ bhavatekṣiteti niviḍaṃ saṃyamya bāhvoḥ srajā
children.translated_text: 'Indeed, she has been seen by you!' — binding [him] tightly with a garland [around] his arms;

children.text: bhūyo drakṣyasi tāṃ śaṭheti dayitaṃ saṃtarjya saṃtarjya ca
children.translated_text: 'You shall see her again, O rogue!' — threatening and threatening the beloved;

children.text: ālīnāṃ pura eva nihnuti-paraḥ kopād raṇan-nūpuraṃ
children.translated_text: already concealed [in hiding] and hell-bent on denial — in anger, with tinkling anklets,
through the procedure of kicking, the proud woman made the beloved into an <s>aśoka</s> tree [struck by a woman's foot to bloom].
The <s>mugdhā</s> (naive woman) is considered of one nature,
as is the <s>punarbhū</s> (remarried woman) — because between these two
the distinction is so extremely subtle
that poets have not demonstrated [it].
The <s>madhyā</s> (moderate) and the <s>pragalbhā</s> (bold) —
she is divided into two:
one is the senior wife (<s>jyeṣṭhā</s>), the other the junior (<s>kaniṣṭhā</s>),
with respect to the hero's affection.
Due to entreaty and affection,
even the hero, though still in love [with another],
generally behaves toward her
as one skilled in the arts — as follows:
'A bee, thinking your eyes to be blue lotuses,

children.text: ruṇadhmy ahaṃ tad iti nimīya locane
children.translated_text: is troublesome! Therefore I close [your] eyes' —
saying this, upon her with cheeks bristling with horripilation,
the young man secretly kissed the other woman.
In prosperity and in adversity,
even in death, she who does not abandon [him] —
she is one's own (<s>svīyā</s>); toward her, love
arises for the meritorious one.
The other's [woman] is said to be twofold:
a maiden and a married woman, O beloved;
[she becomes dear] from seeing or from hearing —
when one is afflicted by desire, as follows:

children.text: kim api lalitaiḥ snigdhaiḥ kiñcit kim apy atikuñcitaiḥ
children.translated_text: With glances that are somehow gentle and affectionate, somehow very curved,

children.text: kim api valitaiḥ kandarpeṣūn hasadbhir ivekṣaṇaiḥ
children.translated_text: somehow turned — as if laughing at <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Love's) arrows —
thus did a new woman look at the desired face,
so that even one skilled in graceful arts was greatly astonished by the friend's look.

children.text: niśamayya bahir manoharaṃ svaram aikṣiṣṭa tathāparā yā &
children.translated_text: Another woman, hearing from outside a captivating voice, looked thus — and afterward, not even a sesame seed's [gap remained], the lotus-eyed one having [seen him through] hearing.

children.text: kasyāścit subhaga iti śrutaś ciraṃ yas taṃ
children.translated_text: One who had long been heard of as handsome — having seen him,
with passion attained, her eyes closed,
her body motionless — seeing this, the attendants
of the bride were distressed, their minds anxious.
Even one merely heard of can cause
emaciation, sleeplessness, and burning;
why does the heart wish to see
that very unattainable beloved?
In person, in a painting, and in a dream —
his seeing may be threefold;
and through place, time, and manner —
his hearing [may also be threefold], as follows:

children.text: satyaṃ santi gṛhe gṛhe priyatamā yeṣāṃ bhujāliṅgana
children.translated_text: 'Truly, in every house there are beloveds whose arm-embraces
produce pure, enchanting waters of [passion], the doe-eyed ones!

children.text: preyān ko'py aparo'yam atra sukṛtī dṛṣṭe'pi yasmin vapuḥ
children.translated_text: Yet this is some other fortunate beloved — merely on seeing whom, the body
attains a certain [condition] manifested through sweat, yawning, trembling, and timidity of the eyes.'
'Wonder! Even though in a painting, this one,
O friend, equal to <s>Madana</s> (the god of love),
forcibly uprooting my modesty,
makes my mind yearn!'
When the beloved came to the naive woman (<s>mugdhā</s>) in a dream, from the touch of his hand,
with her body-creeper adorned with horripilation, she revealed [her passion]; then from indignation —

children.text: mā māṃ vallabha saṃspṛśeti sahasā śūnyaṃ vadantī muhuḥ
children.translated_text: 'Do not touch me, O beloved!' — suddenly saying [this] to the void repeatedly,

children.text: sakhyā no hasitā sacintam asakṛt saṃśocitā pratyuta
children.translated_text: she was laughed at by her friend, [but] was rather pitied with thoughtful concern again and again.
'A palace with brightly blazing lamps,
honey with blue lotuses, melodious song —
O dear friend, all this of yours
is fruitful indeed only if he were here.'

children.text: vikasati kairava-nikare sarati ca sarasī-samīraṇo sutanu &
children.translated_text: 'When the cluster of night-lotuses blooms and the breeze from the lake wafts, O slender one, and the sky kisses the moon — without him, what is love like?'

children.text: cambaty ambaram indau tava tena vinā ratiḥ kīdṛk //
ajananir astu dṛśos tava kucayor abhava-niralaṃ bhavatu &
children.translated_text: 'Let there be non-birth for your eyes; let there be complete non-existence for your breasts — if that youth is neither seen nor embraced fully!'

children.text: yadi dṛśyate na sa yuvā nirbharam āliṅgyate no vā //

children.translated_text: A maiden, even when in love, is unable
to see or speak to him openly —
even when he looks at her and addresses her
in private — due to modesty, as follows:

children.text: kāmaṃ na paśyati didṛkṣata eva bhūmnā
children.translated_text: Though she desires to see, she does not look — yet she greatly wishes to;
though spoken to, she does not speak — yet she earnestly wishes to;
in the conflict between modesty and love, with the mind under [love's] control,
the young woman bears this other sentiment — gracefully.
The friend, knowing the heroine's heart,
speaks to the hero;
or the hero [speaks] to her friend —
for the revelation of love, as follows:
'With her slender body bristling, her eyes budding shut with modesty — this maiden, like your night-lily, O man-moon, desires the touch of [your] hand.'

children.text: tava kumudinīva vāñchati nṛ-candra bālā kara-spṛśam //

children.translated_text: 'That these moonbeams burn,
and that these breezes from sleepless lotuses cause fainting,

children.text: yat khidyate tanur iyaṃ ca tad eṣa doṣaḥ
children.translated_text: and that this body is afflicted — this is the fault,
O slender one, of your own friend who is excessively modest.'
When he is not looking, she
gazes at the beloved with wide eyes;
only looking from afar,
she embraces her friend tightly.
Laughing without reason,
she says something to her friend;
with a pretext, she reveals
some beautiful limb.
A garland placed by her friend etc.,
a girdle etc. — she arranges again;
and she performs charming gestures
with beautiful movements of limbs — as follows:

children.text: abhimukha-gate yasminn eva priye bahuśo vada
children.translated_text: When that very beloved approaches, she speaks much
with downcast face, while the doe-eyed one remains silent;

children.text: atha kila valal-līlālokaṃ sa eṣa tathekṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: then indeed, having been looked at with a wave of playful glances,

children.text: katham api yathā dṛṣṭā manye kṛtaṃ śruti-laṅghanam
children.translated_text: [she thinks:] 'Somehow he has seen me, I think — the boundary of hearing has been transgressed!'
With her body-staff turned sideways, her unevenly heaving breasts exposed,
with a breaking pearl necklace, with cheeks glistening with horripilation and perspiration —

children.text: dūrād eva vilokayety abhimate tad vaktra-dattekṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: she looks from afar at the desired one, her gaze fixed on his face;
overcome by irresistible passion, she tightly embraces her companion.

children.text: animittaṃ yad vihasati niṣkāraṇam eva yat sakhīṃ vadati &
children.translated_text: 'That she laughs without cause, that she speaks to her friend without reason — seeing the beloved, this one declares herself to be under his control.'

children.text: dayitaṃ vilokya tad iyaṃ śaṃsati tad adhīnam ātmānam //

children.translated_text: Raising her arm-creeper, graceful with the beauty of manifesting passion at its root,
beautiful with the pearl strand swaying on the surface of her heaving full breasts,
with the sound of the bracelet on her moving fingertip inviting <s>Smara</s> (Love) —
that scratching of the ear by the slender woman, with half-closed eyes, is triumphant!
A lotus-ear-ornament and a girdle — slightly
adjusting these upon seeing the beloved,
she gives to her friend in return,
as if [giving] a dwelling to <s>Smara</s> (Love) in each limb.
With the network of teeth-rays revealed by a pretended yawn,
with a string of pearls hanging, as if in joy at [seeing] the beloved,
with arm-creepers meeting above in an elaborate display of bracelet-arches —
like a beautiful gateway, another [woman] enters the heart in a gathering.
Even another's married wife does everything
when passion is fully aroused;
in desperate circumstances, she courts
the beloved herself — as follows:

children.text: ullaṅghyāḸ sakhī-vacaḥ samucitām utsṛjya lajjām alaṃ
children.translated_text: 'Having transgressed the words of friends, having fully abandoned fitting modesty,

children.text: hitvā bhītibharaṃ nirasya ca nijaṃ saubhāgya-garvaṃ manāk
children.translated_text: having cast off the weight of fear, having slightly dismissed my own pride in good fortune —

children.text: ājñāṃ kevalam eva manmatha-guror ādāya nūnaṃ mayā
children.translated_text: taking solely the command of the teacher of Love (<s>Manmatha</s>) —
O crest-jewel in the count of all amorous men, I have surely resorted to you!'
The eyes close with bliss,
the hips overflow [with moisture],
and the slender body trembles
Her [state] upon seeing him is as follows:
With closing, languid eyes; with [her sash] slipping as her hand fumbles at the girdle;
with limbs arrested by trembling from the flow of intense passion of <s>Anaṅga</s> (the Bodiless One, i.e., Kāma);
though the flatterer [i.e., her beloved] is before all her limbs, the weak woman, eager at the tryst,

children.text: dāstāṃ rantum aho nirīkṣitum api preyān na sambhāvitaḥ
children.translated_text: was unable even to look at her beloved — alas! — let alone to sport with him.
She does not approach him herself, though fair,
out of naivety, even though distressed [with longing];
but her friend should describe her condition
to the beloved — as follows:
In her sighs, the plantain-leaf fan falters; from the heat,

children.text: nnetrāmbhobhiś cham iti patitaiḥ sicyate ca stanāntaḥ
children.translated_text: with tears from her eyes falling with a 'splash,' the space between her breasts is watered;

children.text: tasyāḥ kiñcit subhaga tad abhūt tānavaṃ tvad-viyoge
children.translated_text: O fortunate one, such has become her thinness in your absence
that suddenly a ring takes the path of a bracelet [on her wasted finger].
One's own wife has no other refuge;
another man's wife is won by wealth;
but the [courtesan's] only [bond] is love —
therefore she is prized by the passionate.
The common woman is the courtesan (<s>veśyā</s>);
she desires only wealth.
There is no hatred [in her] even toward one without merit,
nor attachment even toward one with merit.
This is declared to be her true nature
by some; we, however, say:
even their capacity for love
is described with this reasoning.
In these [courtesans], it is a semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment),
never true <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.
Or else, is their activity [that of] <s>Smara</s> (Love)? —
has Love been devoured by herons? [i.e., is Love extinct?]
Therefore, among them too, in some cases,
there may be passion — but is it in every case?
With feigned emotions for the sake of wealth,
they delude the rustic.
A disguised man [pretending to be an ascetic], one with hidden desires,
one who considers himself manly, a eunuch,
a fool who has easily obtained wealth,
one proud of inherited riches —
such rustics they first
identify and then extract their wealth;
as if [the courtesans were] unprecedented [lovers], they abandon them
and also torment them.
But since they are skilled in the art of amorous play,
their delightful
lovemaking, which makes one forget other women,
arises as follows:
With breast-slopes pressed in tight embrace, with cheeks moist with perspiration,
with lips bitten and sighs released, with brows whirling and hands dancing,
marked by speech that is mostly flattery and various utterances and reached cries —

children.text: veśyānāṃ dhṛti-dhāma puṣpa-dhanuṣaḥ prāpnoti dhanyo ratam
children.translated_text: the fortunate one attains the lovemaking of courtesans, the abode of <s>Manmatha</s>'s (the Flower-Bowed One's) composure.
There is no jealousy for the hero regarding well-born women;
no unhindered sport with another's wife;
but with courtesans, both of these flourish —
they are the very all of <s>Smara</s> (Love), alas!
Formerly reduced to ashes by the fire-flame
of angry <s>Pinākin</s>'s (<s>Śiva</s>'s) eye,
<s>Kāma</s> (Love) is revived again,
I think, by the glances of courtesans.
When served [skillfully], they delight;
otherwise, they destroy.
Inscrutable by nature —
therefore courtesans are comparable to poison.
The <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> (she whose lord is under her control), the <s>utkā</s> (the anxiously waiting one),
likewise the <s>vāsakasajjikā</s> (she who has adorned the bedchamber),
the <s>sandhitā</s> (the reconciled one), the <s>vipralabdhā</s> (the deceived one),
the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (the enraged one), and the <s>abhisārikā</s> (she who goes to meet her lover),
and the <s>proṣitapreyasī</s> (she whose beloved is away) — thus,
the heroines have been previously indicated.
These same eight apply here
according to their conditions, as follows:
She whose husband, drawn by the qualities of love-play,
does not leave her side,
she who is devoted to varied amorous play —
she is the <s>svādhīnapatikā</s>, as follows:

children.text: likhati kucayoḥ patraṃ kaṇṭhe niyojayati srajaṃ
children.translated_text: He paints leaf-designs on her breasts, places a garland at her throat,

children.text: tilakam alike kurvan gaṇḍād udasyati kuntalān
children.translated_text: making a <s>tilaka</s> on her forehead, brushes the curls from her cheek;

children.text: iti caṭu-śatair vāraṃ vāraṃ vapuḥ paritaḥ spṛśan
children.translated_text: thus, with hundreds of flatteries, touching her body all around, again and again,
tormented by separation, her beloved does not leave her side.
She becomes the <s>utkā</s> (anxiously waiting one) — she whose
beloved has not come to the tryst;
anxiously pondering the reason
for his not coming — as follows:

children.text: kiṃ ruddhaḥ priyayā kayācid athavā sakhyā tayodvejitaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Is he detained by some beloved? Or provoked by some friend?

children.text: kiṃ vā kāraṇa-gauravaṃ kim api yan nādyāgato vallabhaḥ
children.translated_text: Or is there some weighty reason why my beloved has not come today?'

children.text: ity ālocya mṛgīdṛśā karatale saṃsthāpya vaktrāmbujaṃ
children.translated_text: Thus reflecting, the doe-eyed one, resting her lotus-face upon her palm,

children.text: dīrghe niḥśvasitaṃ ciraṃ ca ruditaṃ kṣiptāś ca puṣpa-srajaḥ
children.translated_text: sighed long, wept for a long time, and cast away the flower-garlands.
She is the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (one who has adorned the love-chamber) —
she who has adorned her body and the love-chamber,
having heard of her husband's arrival at night,
and gazes intently at the door — as follows:
Having seen her own face in the mirror-disc, the captivating adornment,
and the love-chamber golden with lamplight, with doe-like trembling eyes,

children.text: evaṃ nau surataṃ bhaviṣyati cirād adyeti sānandayā
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'After so long, such will be our lovemaking today!' — with joy,
with desire to see her beloved, she gently casts her most graceful gaze toward the door.
She by whom the beloved was rejected in anger,
even though he bowed [in supplication];
greatly distressed without him — she, [when reconciled],
is called the <s>sandhitā</s> (reconciled one) — as follows:

children.text: yat-pāda-praṇataḥ priyaḥ paruṣayā vācā sa nirvārito
children.translated_text: That her beloved fell at her feet — yet she drove him away with harsh words;

children.text: yat-sakhyā na kṛtaṃ vaco jaḍatayā yan-manyur eko dhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: that her friend's advice was not heeded — in stubbornness; that anger alone was maintained —

children.text: pāpasyāsya phalaṃ tad etad adhunā yac candanendu-dyuti
children.translated_text: the fruit of that sin is this now: that her body, [radiant as] moonlit sandal[-paste],
is repeatedly burned by snow-water, breezes, lotuses, and their fragrance.
She who, having herself sent a go-between and given
a tryst, [finds that] her beloved has not come;
she who is distressed without him —
she is the <s>vipralabdhā</s> (deceived one) — as follows:

children.text: yat saṅketa-gṛhaṃ priyeṇa kathitaṃ sampreṣya dūtīṃ svayaṃ
children.translated_text: The tryst-house that was named by her beloved, having sent a go-between herself —

children.text: tac chūnyaṃ suciraṃ niṣevya sudṛśā paścāc ca bhagnāśayā
children.translated_text: that [house] she frequented empty for a long time, the fair-eyed one, and afterward, with hopes shattered,
with eyes from which thick collyrium flows — indicating her long vigil at the place —

children.text: bhūmāv akṣaramālikeva likhitā dīrghaṃ rudatyā śanaiḥ
children.translated_text: weeping long and slowly, she [traced] on the ground like a garland of letters.
She whose beloved has not come from somewhere
at the expected time of his return;
she who is tormented by his non-arrival —
she is called the <s>khaṇḍitā</s> (enraged one) — as follows:

children.text: sotkaṇṭhaṃ ruditaṃ sakampam asakṛd yātaṃ sa-bāṣpaṃ ciraṃ
children.translated_text: With longing she wept trembling, walked about tearfully for a long time,

children.text: cakṣur dikṣu niveśitaṃ sa-karuṇaṃ sakhyā samaṃ jalpitam
children.translated_text: cast her eyes in all directions, spoke pitifully with her friend;
though the time for his expected return has come, the beloved does not arrive — by the anxious doe-eyed one

children.text: tat tat kiṃcid anuṣṭhitaṃ mṛgadṛśā no yatra vācāṃ gatiḥ
children.translated_text: this and that was done — [acts] where words cannot reach.
She who is made thoroughly shameless
by passion in the matter of love,
and goes [herself] to meet her beloved — she is known as
the <s>abhisārikā</s> (she who goes forth) — as follows:

children.text: no bhītaṃ taḍito dṛśā jalamucā tad-darśanākāṅkṣayā
children.translated_text: She did not fear lightning from the rain-cloud — out of longing to see him;

children.text: no garjir gaṇitā bhṛśaṃ śruti-mukhaṃ tad-vāci saṃcintya ca
children.translated_text: she did not heed the thunder — thinking of his voice at her ear;

children.text: dhārāpātasamudbhavā na ca matā pīḍā tad-āliṅganaṃ
children.translated_text: she did not regard the pain from the downpour — longing for his embrace;
for the slender one in the act of going to meet her beloved — [there was] only that, only that [on her mind].
She whose husband has gone to another land
for some reason,
having set a date — she, greatly afflicted,
is the <s>proṣitapreyasī</s> (she whose beloved is away) — as follows:
Tossing up the disheveled garland of her locks, with cheeks grown pale,
slightly raising her hands out of fear that her loose bracelets might fall,
her vine-like body seated at the door-pillar,
her gaze fixed on the road watching — by some fortunate soul that woman is [at that moment] embraced.
The sighing, the heat, the words of a friend, the intensity,
the anxiety, tears, and the like — accompanied by sorrow —
should be described: the deceived one, the one whose husband has not come, the anxiously waiting one,
the reconciled one [share these], together with the enraged one, in this context.
Adorned with various ornaments and joyful
is the <s>svādhīnabhartṛkā</s> (she whose husband is under her control);
and likewise the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (adornment-ready one) —
but hers is a love that is yet to arrive.
A well-born woman, another man's wife, a courtesan —
the <s>abhisārikā</s> (she who goes forth) is threefold.
Just as [these eight types] have been stated, so too the others —
the <s>svādhīnapatikā</s> and the rest [apply to all three classes].
The well-born one goes concealed, timid,
bashful, and swiftly,
unobserved from all sides,
to the hero — another man's wife [likewise].
Accompanied by a friend, with eyes wide from intoxication,
unsuspecting, without fear,
with jingling ornaments — the courtesan
eagerly goes to meet the hero.
The one's-own-wife type is thirteen-fold;
another's wife is twofold;
the courtesan is one; and furthermore the eight
conditions [apply to each] — differentiated thus.
And again, all of them are threefold:
superior, middling, and inferior.
Thus their total [number]
is three hundred and eighty-four.
She whose anger is proportionate to the fault,
who is pleased when conciliated,
and is deeply attached to her lord,
won by [his] virtues — she is the superior one, as follows:

children.text: kānte kiṃ kupitāsi kaḥ para-jane prāṇeśa kopo bhavet
children.translated_text: 'Beloved, why are you angry?' 'What anger could there be toward a stranger, O lord of my life?'

children.text: ko'yaṃ subhru paras tvam eva dayite dāso'smi kas te paraḥ
children.translated_text: 'Who is this other man, O fair-browed one?' 'You alone, darling.' 'I am your slave — who is another to you?'

children.text: ity uktvā praṇataḥ priyaḥ kṣititalād utthāpya sānandayā
children.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the beloved bowed — raised from the ground by the joyful
slender woman, he was placed upon her breast-slope marked with tear-drops.
She who is angry even at a slight fault,
who releases [anger] with difficulty,
who comes to love out of pity —
she is considered the middling one, as follows:
Though her lips quiver widely, though drops of perspiration
glisten on her blooming cheeks, though she is adorned with very arched brow-play,

children.text: pādāntaḥ-praṇate priye prakaṭayaty antaḥ prasādaṃ priyā
children.translated_text: when her beloved falls at her feet, the dear one reveals inner satisfaction,
slowly loosening the curls wound about [her fingers, which were symbols of] her pique.
She who is angry without cause,
who shows affection without conciliation,
whose conduct is without reason
and whose mind is fickle — she is the inferior one.
Where the tale of <s>Kāma</s>'s (Love's) flower-bow is put to shame, where the play of whirling brows [reigns],
where the cheek's radiance, just arisen, conquers the moon's beauty,
where the necklace on the breast-slope has its glory erased by drops of perspiration —
'Who is this, O proud one, who turns away from my salutation with freshly-seized pride?'
By birth, time, age, condition,
emotion, <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), and the type of hero,
the other [types] would be innumerable —
they are not stated, out of fear of prolixity.
Having known all this and so forth,
and having oneself observed the experts [in the field],
all these [heroines] should be understood
through the distinctive expression of poets.
Horripilation, trembling, paralysis,
perspiration, tears, and bewilderment —
should be described by the poet in <s>saṃyoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (union-erotic sentiment)
as pertaining to the heroine.
The women of relatives, friends, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, kings, harsh men,
and those of higher <s>varṇa</s> (caste) should not be approached;
likewise [those who are] deformed, renunciants, or those whose
secrets are exposed — [this is known] by those who understand <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, and <s>kāma</s>.
By this method, elaborating this especially delightful
<s>saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment of union),
a poet becomes one who relishes emotion and <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic flavor),
delighting in the charming [compositions pleasing to] the assemblies of the learned and to women.

children.text: iti śrī-rudra-bhaṭṭa-viracite śṛṅgāra-tilakābhidhāne kāvya-rasālaṅkāre sambhoga-śṛṅgāro nāma prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, called <s>saṃbhoga-śṛṅgāra</s> (Erotic Sentiment in Union), in the <s>Śṛṅgāratilaka</s> (Ornament of the Erotic), a [treatise on] poetic <s>rasa</s> and <s>alaṅkāra</s> (figures of speech), composed by the illustrious <s>Rudrabhaṭṭa</s>.
(2) Second Chapter
This [erotic sentiment] called <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) is fourfold:
<s>pūrvānurāga</s> (initial love), that called <s>māna</s> (lovers' quarrel), <s>pravāsa</s> (absence), and that whose nature is <s>karuṇā</s> (pathos).
When mutual love arises in a couple from mere sight,

children.text: jñeyaḥ pūrvānurāgo'yam aprāptau ca daśā yathā //
children.translated_text: this should be known as <s>pūrvānurāga</s> (initial love); and when [they are] unable to attain [each other], the stages [are] as follows:
'Why do you prepare a bed of lotus-stalks with sandal-paste?
O my friend, do not, do not make the soft palm-leaf fan for me!
Release your effort in arranging blossoming lotuses! —
only union with him extinguishes the fire of love.'

children.text: yat sārair iva paṅkajasya ghaṭitaṃ yac candra-garbhād iva
children.translated_text: That which is fashioned as if from the essence of the lotus, that which seems to have emerged from the womb of the moon,
that which is enhanced as if by the gleam of <s>Anaṅga</s>'s (Love's) arrow-tip,

children.text: yat saṃsicya sudhā-rasair iva rater āsthāna-bhūmīkṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: that which, sprinkled as if with nectar-juice, has become the throne of <s>Rati</s> (Pleasure) —

children.text: tad bhūyo'pi kadā saroruha-dṛśaḥ paśyāmi tasyā mukham
children.translated_text: when again shall I see the face of that lotus-eyed woman?
Lotus-stalks, plantain, the moon,
sandal, water, lotuses, and the like —
for these two [lovers], none of these [cooling things] served
to pacify the affliction of love.
For those two whose minds are agitated
by love grown from glances and conversation,
when they have not attained [each other],
love progresses through ten stages, as follows:
Desire (<s>abhilāṣa</s>), then reflection (<s>cintā</s>),
recollection (<s>smṛti</s>), and the praise of virtues (<s>guṇakīrtana</s>),
then agitation (<s>udvega</s>), then delirium (<s>pralāpa</s>),
then madness (<s>unmāda</s>) and illness (<s>vyādhi</s>).
Stupor (<s>jaḍatā</s>), and death (<s>maraṇa</s>) —
the tenth — surely arises.
These ten stages occur for those two
when they have not attained [each other] — as follows:
Where there is a resolve
— a strong desire for union with that [beloved] —
from the mind being agitated with longing,
that is called <s>abhilāṣa</s> (desire) — as follows:

children.text: praviśati yathā gehe'kasmād bahiś ca viceṣṭate
children.translated_text: How she enters the house suddenly and restlessly moves about outside,

children.text: vadati ca yathā sakhyā sārdhaṃ sahāsam ihotsukā
children.translated_text: and how she speaks eagerly with her friend, with laughter;

children.text: dayita-vadanāloke mandaṃ yathā ca calaty asau
children.translated_text: and how, at the sight of the beloved's face, she gently moves —

children.text: mṛga-dṛśi tathaitasyāṃ manye smareṇa kṛtaṃ padam
children.translated_text: in this doe-eyed one, I think, <s>Smara</s> (Love) has set his mark.
'How may that beloved be attained?
What should I do for its accomplishment?
How may he be brought under [my] control?' —
such is considered <s>cintā</s> (anxious reflection) — as follows:

children.text: satyaṃ durlabha eṣa vallabhatamo rāgo mamāsmin punaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Truly, this most beloved one is hard to attain; yet my passion for him

children.text: ko'py anyo'sti gurur na cātinipuṇāḥ sakhyo'sya saṃbodhane
children.translated_text: 'There is no other teacher who is supremely skillful in instructing him' —

children.text: saṃcintyeti mṛgīdṛśā priyatame dṛṣṭe ślathāṃ mekhalāṃ
children.translated_text: thinking thus, the doe-eyed woman, when the dearest one is seen, while tying her loosened girdle,

children.text: badhnantyā na gataṃ sthitaṃ na ca galad-vāso na vā saṃvṛtam
children.translated_text: neither went nor stayed, nor [held] the slipping garment, nor covered [herself].
Where there is aversion toward other activities,
the mind being solely focused on that [beloved],
with sighs and daydreams —
those behaviors constitute <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance), as follows:

children.text: induṃ nindati padma-kandala-dalais talpaṃ na vā manyate
children.translated_text: She reviles the moon, does not regard the bed [spread] with lotus-petal shoots,

children.text: karpūraṃ kirati prayāti na ratiṃ prāleya-dhārā-gṛhe
children.translated_text: scatters camphor, finds no pleasure in the hall of snow-streams,

children.text: śvāsaiḥ kevalam eva khedita-tanur dhyāyaty asau bālikā
children.translated_text: with body exhausted by sighs alone, this girl meditates —

children.text: yat tat ko'pi yuvā dhruvaṃ smara-suhṛc-cetasy amuṣāḥ sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: surely some youth, a friend of <s>Smara</s> (Love), is fixed in the mind of this one.
Where there is speech [saying]: 'In beauty, laughter, and conversation
there is no other youth equal to him' —
that is called <s>guṇa-kīrtana</s> (praising of virtues),
as follows:
'That face of his is a moon-orb with a smile, that gaze of his is expansive,

children.text: sā vāṇī jita-kāma-kārmuka-ravā saundaryam etasya tat
children.translated_text: that voice conquers the sound of <s>Kāma</s>'s bow, such is his beauty' —
thus continuously, O friend, [she speaks], her mind absorbed in meditation on the dearest one —

children.text: cetaś cumbita-kāla-kūṭam iva me kasmād idaṃ muhyati
children.translated_text: 'Why does this mind of mine swoon, as if having tasted <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison)?'
Where, whether pleasant or unpleasant,
nothing gives rise to joy,
there is aversion even toward living —
that is called <s>udvega</s> (agitation), as follows:
You perceive the moon before you as fire-shaped, like a <s>cakravākī</s> bird;
you burn trembling from the cool wind, like a lotus-plant;

children.text: prāṇān dhatse katham api balād gacchataḥ śalya-tulyāṃ
children.translated_text: you sustain your life-breaths somehow, by force, [life] being like a barb to one departing —

children.text: stat kenāsau sutanu jantio mānmathas te vikāraḥ
children.translated_text: so tell me, O slender one, by whom was this amorous transformation caused in you?
Where the mind wanders here and there
with eagerness for love,
and speech is only about the beloved —
that is called <s>pralāpa</s> (delirious talk), as follows:

children.text: itthaṃ tena nirīkṣitaṃ na ca mayāpy evaṃ samālokitas
children.translated_text: 'Thus he looked [at me], but I did not look at him in that way;

children.text: tenoktaṃ subhagena tatra na mayā dattaṃ vaco mandayā
children.translated_text: that fortunate one spoke there, but I, being slow, gave no reply' —

children.text: tat satyaṃ kathayāli kiṃ sa subhagaḥ kupyen na mahyaṃ gata
children.translated_text: 'Tell me truly, friend — would that fortunate one not be angry with me?' —

children.text: ity uktvā sudṛśā kayāpi valita-grīvaṃ dṛśau sphārite
children.translated_text: saying this, some fair-eyed woman turned her neck, with eyes wide-open.
Where activity arises consisting of
sighs, weeping, trembling,
and scratching the ground —
that is called <s>unmāda</s> (madness), as follows:
The princess, with unblinking eyes, scratches the ground, sighs loudly,

children.text: kiṃcid dhyāyati niścalā ca balavad romāñcitā kampate
children.translated_text: meditates somewhat, [sits] motionless, trembles greatly with horripilation,

children.text: rodity aṅga-gatāṃ vilokya suciraṃ vīṇām api vyāpṛtā
children.translated_text: weeps, and gazes long at the <s>vīṇā</s> resting on her body, being occupied [with it] —

children.text: svalpair eva dinair iyaṃ vara-tanuḥ kenāpi saṃśikṣitā
children.translated_text: in just a few days, this one of excellent body has been trained by someone.
Predominantly characterized by the sensation of burning,
troubled by long sighs,
the body made thin — this eighth [stage]
is called <s>vyādhi</s> (sickness), as follows:
The heat has dried the sandal-paste water; the sighs have scattered the lotuses;
a paleness fierce enough to overpower camphor [has appeared] on the cheek-surface;
the body has attained thinness — delicate as a withering young lotus-stalk.

children.text: tanv-aṅgyāḥ kathitaḥ smareṇa guruṇā ko'py eṣa kaṣṭa-kramaḥ
children.translated_text: Some terrible sequence has been inflicted upon this slender-limbed one by the grave [god] <s>Smara</s>.
Where there is a sudden 'hum' sound,
the gaze fixed, memory gone,
sighs excessive, emaciation —
this is considered <s>jaḍatā</s> (stupor), as follows:
The gaze has motionless pupils; the lower lip is made ashen by sighs;
the face has attained the state of a daytime moon-disc; memory is destroyed;

children.text: huṃkāraḥ param eka eva vacana-sthāne sthitaḥ sāṃprataṃ
children.translated_text: only a single 'hum' sound remains now in place of speech —
I think the flower-weaponed [<s>Kāma</s>] has encamped with his army in every limb of hers.
If by various means the woman
does not achieve union,
then for her, pierced by <s>Kandarpa</s>'s arrows,
death occurs.
These ten stages arise
for men too, from love;
but death [as the tenth stage], due to [men's] lack of beauty,
is not depicted by some [poets] for them.
Others do depict it too,
with the expectation of revival;
in narration of past events, that is commendable;
in original composition, generally not.
Even if one of the two dies,
if the other somehow lives,
what reckoning of love is there?
One should die if there is no union.
First the woman should be enamored,
the man afterwards — through her gestures;
then the play of union —
this is the naturally auspicious arrangement.
Even otherwise there is no fault,
if the love of both is equal;
but if one is enamored and the other not,
that is merely a semblance of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment).
And this is generally depicted by connoisseurs
thus in comic [compositions]:
'O courtesan, with me who have no wealth,
honor [your] youth!'
The hero, being enamored of a woman,
her circle of friends —
by conciliation, respect, and gifts
he earnestly wins over.
Speaking of her [the beloved] before them [the friends],
he reveals his own intention;
in her [the friend's] absence, he should employ
certain female ascetics and the like.
Through that channel, having declared his nature
and ascertained her mind,
with attentions, other [gestures], and letters,
he should win her without slackness.
Then, seeing her in private,
through magic tricks, arts, and the like,
with charming devices, at ease,
he should lead her to supreme wonder.
In the house of a nurse or friend, on a night-outing,
at a great festival, in an intense [moment of] fear,
by invitation, under the pretext of illness, in an empty
house — their first meeting should take place.
When desire is intense and she
cannot be obtained even when asked,
the hero, his means exhausted, should then
win the maiden [by force] — thus [it is taught].
The method of approaching another's wife
is not prescribed by poets;
but as a beautiful element of poetry,
it is depicted — therefore:
The coyness of women, their inaccessibility,
and their resistance —
that itself I consider to be
the supreme weapon of the five-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>].
Out of great respect or even fear,
a man's concealed desire for another woman
becomes charming [in poetry],
even for virtuous persons — as follows:
A dilapidated straw hut is the dwelling; the bed is made on bare ground;

children.text: nīrandhraṃ timiraṃ kiranti salilaṃ garjanta ete ghanāḥ
children.translated_text: impenetrable darkness, these clouds pour water and rumble;

children.text: gacchāmīti vadaty asāv api muhuḥ śaṅkākulā kevalaṃ
children.translated_text: 'I am going,' she says repeatedly, merely distressed with apprehension —

children.text: cetaś citram aho tathāpi ramate saṃketake kāminām
children.translated_text: wonderful! The mind nonetheless delights at the rendezvous of lovers.
That is called <s>māna</s> (love-anger) wherein the heroine
out of jealousy toward the hero
assumes an altered [state], due to the fault
of his association with another woman — as follows:
The eyes slightly adorned with tear-water, contracted,
a redness shown on the cheeks, beautiful with the accompaniment of throbbing,
a trembling fashioned on the bud of the lower lip — by the doe-eyed one;

children.text: no jāne kim ayaṃ priye prakaṭitaḥ kopo'bhilāṣo'thavā
children.translated_text: I do not know, O dear one, whether this that is displayed is anger or desire.
That [<s>māna</s>] is generally threefold
in women toward their beloved,
depending on the perceived offense:
heavy, moderate, and light.
When the lover has gone to another woman,
[or is] seen himself with nail-marks,
[or] upon seeing her garment,
[or] a slip of the [wrong] name — the heavy [anger is], as follows:

children.text: bimboṣṭhaḥ sphurati prayāti paṭutāṃ gaṇḍa-sthale śoṇimā
children.translated_text: The <s>bimba</s>-fruit lip quivers; on the cheek-surface the redness intensifies;

children.text: yātas tiryag amū dṛśau ca balavad bhrū-yugmaam udbhrāmyati
children.translated_text: those two eyes have gone oblique, and the brow-pair vigorously arches;

children.text: itthaṃ caṇḍi tathā tavaiṣa ruciraḥ kopa-kramo jṛmbhate
children.translated_text: 'Thus, O fierce one, this beautiful sequence of your anger swells —

children.text: jāto'yaṃ praṇatīr apāsya sutarām etad-didṛkṣur yathā
children.translated_text: it has arisen, casting aside [my] bows, all the more as if desiring to see this [spectacle].'
When the dearest one is seen with desire
conversing with another woman,
or when a fault is reported by a friend —
this is the moderate <s>māna</s>, as follows:

children.text: vāco vāgmini kiṃ tavādya paruṣāḥ subhru bhruvor vibhramai
children.translated_text: 'Why are your words harsh today, O eloquent one? O fair-browed one, why the play of eyebrows?

children.text: rviśrāntaṃ kuta eva lola-nayane kiṃ lohite locane
children.translated_text: Whence this rest, O restless-eyed one? Why are the eyes reddened?

children.text: svedaḥ kiṃ nu ghanastani stana-taṭe muktā-phalānāṃ tulāṃ
children.translated_text: Why does the perspiration on the chest-surface of you, O full-breasted one, rival pearls?

children.text: dhatte muñca ruṣaṃ mamātra dayite leśo'pi nāsty āgasaḥ
children.translated_text: Release your anger — O my beloved, there is not even a trace of offense in me.'
When the beloved looks coquettishly
at another woman with sparkling eyes,
being slightly absent-minded —
the light [<s>māna</s>] arises, as follows:

children.text: mām eva tāḍaya nitambini yady akasmāt
children.translated_text: 'Strike me alone, O full-hipped one, if suddenly

children.text: kopo bhavet tava mukhaṃ tu nijaṃ kim etat
children.translated_text: there should be anger in you — but why this, your own face
being brought to resemble the moon — cheek
flooded with the stream of thick collyrium from the eyes?'
Due to circumstances of place and time, anger
generally arises in all women;
it is either easy to appease
or difficult to appease by lovers.
A love-chamber ablaze with brilliant lamps, and a palace-terrace bright with the moon,
and a lotus-grove awakened by the sweet hum of bees maddened by honey —
in such places and the like,
the doubt [as to whether she is] a sulking woman [is resolved —]
even very heavy anger
quickly becomes easy to appease, as follows:
In spring-time, at moonrise, and at times when the intoxication of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love) is excessive,
the <s>māna</s> of proud women becomes very easy to appease, due to [its] abundance.

children.text: dūtī-janasya parato laghur api doṣo gurūyate prāyaḥ &
children.translated_text: From messengers' [reports], even a slight fault of the other is usually magnified;
similarly, on the occasion of a fresh offense, [it is so] for women too — as follows:
Conciliation (<s>sāma</s>), gifts (<s>dāna</s>), and division (<s>bheda</s>),
disregard (<s>upekṣā</s>) and prostration (<s>praṇati</s>),
and the disruption of the occasion (<s>prasaṅga-vidhvaṃsa</s>),
[but not] punishment (<s>daṇḍa</s>), for it destroys <s>śṛṅgāra</s>.
For her appeasement, the wise have declared
six means;
they are beautifully illustrated
together with examples, as follows:
'Even though I am undisciplined, I am to be protected
by you, O fair-browed one, who are endowed with forbearance' —
where such speech occurs,
that is called <s>sāma</s> (conciliation).
Where the hero gives ornaments and the like
for [her] satisfaction,
pointing to some reason —
that is <s>dāna</s> (gift), [effective] with greedy [women], as follows:
Where, having won over her retinue
through graciousness,
he obtains the beloved through them —
that is called <s>kāntā-bheda</s> (division of the beloved['s resistance]).
Abandoning the method of appeasement,
where the woman is appeased by words
hinting at other meanings —
that is considered <s>upekṣā</s> (disregard), as follows:

children.text: etat kiṃ nanu karṇa-bhūṣaṇa-mayaṃ hāraḥ sukāñcī navā
children.translated_text: 'What is this — an ear-ornament-like necklace? A new beautiful girdle

children.text: baddhā kācid iyaṃ tvayādya tilakaḥ ślāghyaḥ priye kalpitaḥ
children.translated_text: has been tied by you today? And this laudable <s>tilaka</s> (forehead-mark) has been made, O dear one!' —
touching [her] limb by limb — at that instant, adorned with a garland of horripilation,

children.text: tanvī mānam upekṣayaiva śanakair dhūrtena saṃmocitā
children.translated_text: the slender one's <s>māna</s> was slowly released by the rogue through disregard alone.
Resorting to mere humility,
prostration at [her] feet is considered [<s>praṇati</s>];
it is greatly desired by women,
and is charming — as follows:
Where suddenly there arises
an experience of fear, joy, and the like —
this is <s>prasaṅga-vidhvaṃsa</s> (disruption of the occasion),
whose nature is the shattering of anger — as follows:
'How did this arrow with its wing-sound
fall on my chest?' — when the beloved spoke thus,

children.text: nivṛtya kiṃ kim idam iti bruvāṇayā
children.translated_text: turning back [she asked] 'What? What is this?' —
thus fearfully the angry beloved was observed [relenting].
Each successive [method] is stronger —
these are the means of appeasement;
the first three should be used frequently
by the clever; the latter ones only sometimes.
The beloved should not be excessively vexed
by the woman at any time;
and <s>māna</s> should be made rare,
for the success of the festival of prostration.
The heroine too should employ these means
toward the beloved;
but the well-born woman does not show jealousy —
there the cause would be something else.
Without affection there is no fear,
nor jealousy without love;
therefore this mode of <s>māna</s>
reveals the love of both.
<s>Priya</s>, <s>subhaga</s>, <s>dayita</s>, <s>vallabha</s>, <s>nātha</s>, <s>svāmī</s>, <s>Īśa</s>, <s>kānta</s>, <s>candramukha</s>;

children.text: dayita manorama ramaṇī-jīvita ity ādi nāma syāt //
children.translated_text: 'beloved,' 'charming one,' 'darling,' 'life' — and so forth would be the names.

children.text: prītau bhartari sudṛśām aprītau punar amūni śaṭha-dhṛṣṭau &
children.translated_text: When the husband is pleasing, [women use] these for the fair-eyed ones; when displeasing, then: 'O rogue! O bold one!
O shameless one! O wicked one! O cruel one! O ill-mannered one!' — and so forth.
Through arrogance, abandonment in adversity, displeasing actions, harsh speech,

children.text: lobhād atipravāsāt strīṇāṃ dveṣyaḥ priyo bhavati //
children.translated_text: greed, and excessive absence — the beloved becomes hateful to women.
When the beloved goes to a foreign land
for some reason —
that is known as <s>pravāsa</s> (sojourn abroad),
a painful state for both.

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ ketaka-dhūli-dhūsaram idaṃ vyoma kramād vīkṣitāḥ
children.translated_text: 'The sky is seen grey with <s>ketaka</s>-pollen dust; gradually, the edges of the horizon
bearing mushroom-like shoots have been seen; the <s>kadamba</s>-scented winds have been endured —

children.text: sakhyaḥ saṃvṛṇutāśru muñcata bhayaṃ kasmān mudevākulā
children.translated_text: friends, stop the tears, release the fear! Why are you troubled for no reason?

children.text: etān apy adhunāsmi vajraghaṭitā nūnaṃ sahiṣye dhanān
children.translated_text: Even these thunderbolts I shall surely endure now, for I am [hard as] diamond.'
'Surely the peacocks' cry is harsh to the ears — how can it be exceedingly sweet?
And the clouds, though bearers of ambrosia, are mostly made to drip poison.'
this row of fresh sprouts bursting forth, though endurable, becomes unendurable —

children.text: tat kiṃ yad viparītam atra na kṛtaṃ tasyā viyogena me
children.translated_text: what indeed has not been reversed here by her separation from me!
Emaciation, sleeplessness, pallor,
anxiety, and the like arise therein;
the various conditions of women [in separation] —
death, if it is beyond the limit [of endurance].
Today itself, O friend, you who are [thin as] the crescent moon risen on the first day [of the fortnight] —

children.text: sakhyaṃ tvayā vapur idaṃ gamitaṃ varākyāḥ
children.translated_text: this body of the wretched one has been reduced to this state through your friendship;
when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has departed, O <s>Kusuma-sāyaka</s> (flower-arrowed Kāma), tell me — come morning,
where will you discharge your volley of arrows?

children.text: niḥśvāsaiḥ saha sāmprataṃ sakhi gatā vṛddhiṃ dhruvaṃ rātrayaḥ
children.translated_text: O friend, surely the nights have now grown longer along with my sighs;

children.text: sārdhaṃ locana-vāriṇā vigalitaṃ yat prāktanaṃ me sukham
children.translated_text: and my former happiness has flowed away together with the tears from my eyes;

children.text: prāṇāśā tanutām upaiti ca muhur nūnaṃ tanu-spardhayā
children.translated_text: the hope of [retaining my] life grows thin, surely in rivalry with my body;

children.text: kandarpaḥ param eka eva vijayī yāte'pi kānte sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love) alone remains supremely victorious, standing firm even when my beloved has departed.
The sprout of her lip is without color; her braid is exceedingly disheveled; her eyes are not adorned with collyrium;
her bodily complexion assumes the whiteness of a withering young lotus stalk;

children.text: itthaṃ subhru visaṃsthulāpi viraha-vyāpād vimardād iyaṃ
children.translated_text: thus, O fair-browed one, though differing in form, this [pallor], through the assault of separation's affliction,
has firmly embraced her in every limb, like a friend with steadfast beauty.

children.text: kiṃ tatra nāsti rajanī kiṃ vā candro na suṣṭhu-ruciḥ &
children.translated_text: Is there no night there? Or is the moon not beautiful enough?

children.text: yena sakhi vallabhām api na smarati sa māṃ videśa-ruciḥ //
children.translated_text: That he who delights in foreign lands, O friend, does not even remember his beloved — let alone me! //
Blow, O breeze, spreading the fragrance of the <s>kunda</s> (jasmine); O moon, reveal your desires freely;

children.text: prakaṭaya śaśinn āśāḥ kāmaṃ manoja samullasa
children.translated_text: O <s>Manoja</s> (Love), exult to your heart's content!
The appointed day is past, O friends — abandon talk of him;

children.text: hṛdayam adhunā kiñcit kartuṃ mamānyad ihecchati
children.translated_text: my heart now wishes to do something else here.
Such and other conditions of separation [in love] —
they arise for men too;
the falling of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s arrows and the rest —
may they not befall even enemies!
Where, when one [of the pair] has perished, the other,
though himself nearly dead, speaks with love
to the departed one — that is the hero's lament,
and that is remembered as <s>karuṇa</s> (the pathetic) — as follows:
The plantain-tree of lovely woman's graces is burned; the <s>vīṇā</s> is uprooted;
the moonlight — the elixir of the cool — is swallowed, drunk up by the <s>pañcama</s> (fifth note) cuckoo-cry;
the treasures of many brilliant gems are scorched; love alone is insufficient —

children.text: kandarpaṃ haratā hareṇa bhuvanaṃ niḥsāram etat kṛtam
children.translated_text: by <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) who destroyed <s>Kandarpa</s>, this world is made worthless.

children.text: vaktraṃ candramasā dṛśau mṛga-gaṇaiḥ keśāḥ kalāpi-vrajair
children.translated_text: Her face [has been carried away] by the moon; her eyes by the deer; her hair by the peacock-flocks;
the roundness of her breasts by elephants; the grace of her arms by lotus stalks;

children.text: saugandhyaṃ malayānilena balinā tanvī vibhajyeti sā
children.translated_text: her fragrance by the powerful <s>Malaya</s> breeze — that slender one is thus divided away;

children.text: sarvair niṣkaruṇair hṛtā dhruvam aho daivena kiṃcin na me
children.translated_text: she is surely carried off by all these merciless ones — alas, by fate, nothing is left to me!

children.text: iyatīṃ subhagāvasthāṃ gato'si yasyāḥ kṛte smarātaṅkāt &
children.translated_text: You have reached such a fortunate state — she, for whose sake you suffered the torment of love,

children.text: mūrcchāṃ harāmi sā tava gata-puṇyā nayana-salilena //
children.translated_text: I take away the swoon — she, whose merit is exhausted, [weeps] with tears. //
The noose has been loosened; this thick camphor-powder has been applied;
your chest has been embraced, O drooping-limbed one;
the sinful one by whom you were brought to this state —
as you emerge gracefully from the swoon, cast your gaze upon me.
Exhausted, shedding tears, distressed,
with limbs collapsed, bereft of consciousness,
anxious, partaking of misery — in this [rasa]
people are generally thus.
In some cases, the semblance of <s>karuṇa</s> (pathetic)
arises here from compassion,
forgetting the [actual] condition of that couple
which originates in love.
This [karuṇa semblance] arises for man and woman
when they look toward reunion;
being predominantly the speech of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (the erotic),
it is <s>karuṇa</s> only in a different sense.
Therefore this is truly <s>śṛṅgāra</s> alone,
enhanced by <s>karuṇa</s>;
it bears special beauty,
[yet] is rarely composed by the wise.
A craftswoman, a maidservant, an actress, a nurse,
a female neighbor, and an artisan-woman,
a young girl, and a renunciant woman —
these are to be known as the female friends (<s>sakhīs</s>) of women.
Skill in the arts, enthusiasm,
devotion, knowledge of [the heroine's] mind, memory,
sweetness, knowledge of humor,
and eloquence — these are their qualities.
Entertainment, adornment, instruction,
gentle reproach, and then pacification,
arranging union, and consolation in separation —
these are the duties of a <s>sakhī</s> (female friend), as follows:

children.text: mayā ko'yaṃ mugdhe kathaya likhitaḥ satvara-sakhī
children.translated_text: 'Who is this I have drawn, O innocent one? Tell me quickly!' — the friend's
words being heard, she gazes intently at the painting-board;

children.text: na vaktuṃ tanvaṅgyā śakitam atha coddāma-vidalat
children.translated_text: the slender-limbed one is unable to speak, and then, with profusely blooming
kadamba-like [horripilation], her body itself declared: 'My beloved!'

children.text: pratyaṅgaṃ prati karma narma-parayā kṛtvādhirūḍhaṃ smarā
children.translated_text: With the friend playfully attending to each limb, arousing the eagerness of love,

children.text: dautsukyaṃ pravilokya mohana-vidhau cāturyam ālokya ca
